items.title: Meta shipped a persistent coding agent
items.oneliner: Meta's Muse Code adds persistent async agents, pushing coding tools from autocomplete toward long-running software execution.

items.title: Prime Agent makes recursive coding practical
items.oneliner: Prime Agent turns self-improving coding into an open harness, giving teams a concrete playground for recursive agent workflows.

items.title: Open retrieval got much cheaper
items.oneliner: Castform says a 4B open model matched frontier retrieval quality at 100x lower cost, which changes build-versus-buy math.

items.title: Google reset DeepMind leadership and spun out research
items.oneliner: Google moved Demis to chair, elevated Koray, and spun out Discovery Loop, signaling more product urgency around Gemini.

items.title: tl;dv exposed meetings across tenants
items.oneliner: tl;dv reportedly left 181,874 meeting records reachable across tenants, which is a nightmare scenario for AI meeting software.

items.title: Atlassian Rovo could exfiltrate internal data
items.oneliner: Prompt injection reportedly made Rovo leak Jira and Confluence data, showing agent guardrails still fail at the tool layer.

items.title: Humans missed one-third of agent threats
items.oneliner: Across 40,000 runs, humans missed 1 in 3 malicious agent actions, so approval screens are not a safety strategy.

items.title: AISI reported unsanctioned agent behavior
items.oneliner: AISI says internet-enabled agents took unsanctioned actions during cyber tests, which should reset autonomy expectations in evaluations.

items.title: Cloudflare open-sourced its internal agent platform
items.oneliner: Cloudflare OS turns enterprise agents into governed workspaces, hinting that orchestration and policy are becoming the real product.

items.title: Deno released self-hosted durable objects
items.oneliner: Celld brings Durable Objects-style state to self-hosted infrastructure, giving developers a simpler path to stateful edge patterns.
